clarity.good: A shopper understands the product/message on first reading. Plain natural language, coherent headline and body.
clarity.bad: Jargon, tangled qualification, vague subject, or explanation of how to write instead of finished copy.

visual_specificity.good: Concrete supported objects/actions or a plausible everyday moment the reader can picture. Visual means picturable writing, not evaluation of a generated image.
visual_specificity.bad: Only an inventory list, abstract adjectives or an invented scene asserted as customer evidence.

pain_relevance.good: Recognisable hesitation or practical frustration relevant to this brief, expressed empathetically without fear exploitation.
pain_relevance.bad: Generic parenting reassurance, unrelated problem, exaggerated fear, or identical opening in all variants.

benefit.good: Explains what the relevant supported feature changes for this shopper; a feature-led opening is allowed for informed shoppers.
benefit.bad: Lists contents/policies without explaining relevance, empty life transformation, or an unsupported outcome.

crispness.good: Each sentence earns its place; direct natural wording, useful CTA, no filler or formulaic hype. Necessary qualifications remain concise.
crispness.bad: Repeated catalog lists, padded transitions, vague premium/ultimate/game-changing claims, redundant disclaimers or weak circular CTA.

distinctiveness.good: The three variants offer genuinely different relevant angles or executions within the same facts and brief.
distinctiveness.bad: Three paraphrases of the same product list or synonyms sold as new concepts.

provenance: Editorial operationalisation of source principles plus user preferences. Weights and diversity criterion are design choices, not source-proven metrics.
gate: Material unsupported claims make a candidate not ready, regardless of numeric score.
stopping_rule: One initial revision; at most one additional revision if first fails. No repeated rerolls to obtain a winning score.
limits: AI reviewers, same model family, small sample; scores are editorial proxies, not CTR/CVR/ROAS.
